evidence.source: 漢字ペディア; entry cites 角川新字源 改訂新版
evidence.field: Japanese character readings, meanings, formation, and examples
evidence.text: For Japanese 日, lists on-readings ニチ・ジツ and kun-readings ひ・か; defines sun, daylight, a day, and daily senses, and lists uses such as 日光, 毎日, and 日帰り. Its formation note calls the graph pictographic, depicting the sun, and says it expresses sun, sunlight, and one day. This supports a whole-graph pictogram, not a component split.
evidence.title: 日 | 漢字一字 | 漢字ペディア

evidence.field: 常用漢字表の音訓索引, entry 日
evidence.text: The official table lists 日 with ニチ・ジツ, ひ, and か, and gives examples such as 日時, 日光, 毎日, 連日, 平日, 休日, 日帰り, 月曜日, 三日, and 十日. It separately labels readings in words such as 明日（あす）, 昨日（きのう）, 今日（きょう）, 一日（ついたち）, 二十日（はつか）, 日和（ひより）, and 二日（ふつか）; these are word-level readings, not automatically readings of 日 in isolation.
evidence.kind: official Japanese orthography and reading table
evidence.title: 常用漢字表の音訓索引

evidence.field: 常用漢字表; promulgation and scope
evidence.text: The 2010 常用漢字表 was promulgated on 2010-11-30 as a guide to kanji use in modern Japanese. It is an official current-use reference; it is not, by itself, evidence that 日 underwent a distinct postwar shape change.
evidence.title: 常用漢字表（平成22年内閣告示第2号）

evidence.source: National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics, Kotoba Kenkyukan; author credited as 銭谷真人
evidence.field: Explanation of Japanese new and old forms
evidence.text: The article explains that some characters were standardized in simplified forms by the 1949 当用漢字字体表, with those forms carried into later 常用漢字表 standards. It does not identify 日 as a changed new-form/old-form pair. For 日, the researched evidence supports describing current Japanese 日 as the ordinary graph without asserting a 日-specific shinjitai reform.
evidence.title: 「国」と「國」のように、昔と今とで形がちがう漢字があるのはなぜですか

evidence.source: Kotobank; 精選版 日本国語大辞典 entry 日
evidence.field: Japanese lexical senses, readings, and dated earliest examples
evidence.text: For the Japanese word ひ（日）, reports early cited examples: sun in 古事記 (712); sunlight in 万葉集 (late 8th century); daytime in 古事記 (712); time-unit 一日 in 三教指帰 (c. 797); and a specified date in 竹取物語 (late 9th to early 10th century). The entry also records later senses such as occasion, auspicious day, and weather with examples from 七偏人 (1857–63), 源氏物語 (1001–14), and 土左日記 (c. 935). These are Japanese word attestations, not a chronology for the ancient Chinese graph. The dictionary gives earliest examples available to its compilation, not necessarily absolute first occurrences.
evidence.title: 日(ヒ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.source: Kotobank; 精選版 日本国語大辞典 entry 日
evidence.field: Japanese lexical senses, on-reading にち, and dated examples
evidence.text: The entry lists にち as a reading for sun and for the weekday 日曜, and as a counter for calendar dates and elapsed days. Its cited examples include 日 as the sun in 浮世床 (1813–23), date-counter use in 源氏物語 (1001–14), and elapsed-day counting in 延慶本平家 (1309–10). It identifies the popular on-readings in the character entry as ニチ（呉） and ジツ（漢）; this is a dictionary classification, not evidence for the graph's Chinese formation.
evidence.title: 日(ヒ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.source: Kotobank; 精選版 日本国語大辞典 entry 日本
evidence.field: Japanese use of 日本 and dated attestations
evidence.text: The dictionary explains 日本 as a written form associated with the Japanese expression ひのもと (“place where the sun rises”), and says it was read やまと before increasingly being read ニホン or ニッポン. It cites 日本 in 宇津保物語 (c. 970–999), Nifon in 日葡辞書 (1603–04), and ニッホン in 高野本平家 (13th century). This is the history of the Japanese word/name 日本; it does not establish the date when 日 alone began to abbreviate 日本. The same source says the pronunciation history of 日本 is not settled and gives a possible route through ニチホン to ニッポン and ニホン.
evidence.title: 日本(ニホン)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, The Multi-function Chinese Character Database, CUHK
evidence.field: 形義通解; graph interpretation and cited oracle-bone and bronze uses
evidence.text: Describes 日 as a depiction of the sun; reports round early forms, some squared because circles were difficult to carve on oracle bones, and a central mark said to prevent confusion with 囗. It cites Shang oracle-bone examples for sun/sunrise (合集34163), eclipse (合集11480), daylight contrasted with evening (合集33871, 合集34036), a five-day period (合集12314), and a sacrificial name (合集27463). It also reports bronze-inscription uses for sun, daylight, and calendar-day expressions. These cited uses establish multiple early attestations but not their relative order or all semantic links.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：日

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, The Multi-function Chinese Character Database, CUHK
evidence.text: The oracle-bone component entry identifies 日 as a sun image and reiterates the rounded-to-squared explanation and central mark distinguishing it from 囗. It cites the same Shang-period inscriptions for sun, daylight, day-unit, and sacrificial uses. These are inscription catalogue references, not individually verified absolute dates in this research.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：甲骨部件「日」

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, digitized 說文解字 with 段玉裁 commentary
evidence.field: 卷七 日部; Xu Shen entry and Duan commentary
evidence.text: The received Shuowen entry glosses 日 as 實, describes it as 太陽之精不虧, segments it as 从囗一, and calls it pictographic. Duan Yucai interprets the outer outline as the sun's circumference and the inner stroke as its undiminished center. This is a Han-era lexicographic account with Qing commentary; it is not direct proof that 囗 and 一 were original components of the earlier graph.
evidence.title: 說文解字「日」

evidence.field: File description, source attribution, dating scope, and reuse rights
evidence.text: The page labels the SVG a modern vector depiction of 日 in Western Zhou bronze-script style and cites Xiaoxuetang record 32.EE8F for 師虎簋, described as mid Western Zhou. The page states CC0/public-domain terms and links the original SVG. This asset is a modern redraw of an attributed form, not an image of the original vessel. No upstream Xiaoxuetang character-specific page was successfully opened in this run, and the image pixels were not independently inspected.
evidence.title: File:日-bronze.svg - Wikimedia Commons

gaps: CUHK cites Shang-period inscription catalogue identifiers for sun, daylight, a day-unit, and a sacrificial name but this research did not independently verify each inscription's absolute date. They should be reported as Shang-period examples, not securely dated first occurrences.

The cited early inscriptional uses do not establish whether sun, daylight, and day-unit uses developed in that order, or establish all semantic links among them. Dictionary gloss order is not chronology.

Shuowen's 从囗一 segmentation is a received Han-era interpretation. Earlier evidence supports the graph as a sun depiction, but does not independently establish 囗 and 一 as the graph's original components.
The CUHK account says the inner mark distinguishes 日 from 囗 and attributes some squared forms to carving constraints. The exact emergence and chronology of these graphic details are not established.

Japanese dictionary citations document senses and earliest cited examples for the Japanese word ひ（日） separately from the early Chinese graph attestations. A continuous chronological semantic path between them is not established by the inspected sources.
The Japanese historical dictionary dates the compound 日本 in cited sources and discusses its readings, but the first use of isolated 日 as an abbreviation for 日本 was not established.
No inspected Japanese source identified a distinct traditional 日 form replaced by a Japanese shinjitai 日. The standard reference lists 日 itself; therefore no kyūjitai counterpart is assigned.
The official U+65E5 Unihan record could not be opened. The local kMandarin rì and Baxter–Sagart readings were checked but cannot be emitted as externally verified readings here.

The Commons attribution page identifies a modern drawing and reports CC0, but the Xiaoxuetang record 32.EE8F page returned internal error and the SVG pixels were not independently inspected. Treat the dating/provenance as the Commons page's attributed record rather than direct artifact verification.
